rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet’s analogy of a rider’s cup and instruction to place him at the beginning, middle, and end of supplication.
rows.anchor: قال جابر: قال لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تجعلوني كقدح الراكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report strange and Musa ibn Ubayda weak in hadith.
rows.anchor: فهذا حديث غريب، وموسى بن عبيدة ضعيف الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the Witr qunut supplication as an especially emphasized setting connected with sending blessings on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ذلك: دعاء القنوت: لما رواه الإمام أحمد وأهل السنن، وابن خزيمة

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali reports that the Prophet taught him the Witr supplication beginning with a request for guidance and ending in praise of God.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي، رضي الله عنهما، قال: علمني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمات أقولهن في الوتر

rows.speaker: النسائي
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i's version adds a closing invocation asking God to bless Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وزاد النسائي في سننه بعد هذا: وصلى الله على النبي محمد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recommends frequent blessings upon the Prophet on Friday and its eve.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك: أنه يستحب الإكثار من الصلاة عليه [في] (4) يوم الجمعة وليلة الجمعة:

rows.speaker: أوس بن أوس الثقفي
rows.claim: Aws reports that Friday is the best day, prayers are presented to the Prophet then, and the earth is forbidden to consume prophets’ bodies when asked how prayers reach him after decay.
rows.anchor: عن أوس بن أوس الثقفي، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أفضل أيامكم يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban, al-Daraqutni, and al-Nawawi authenticated the Friday report.
rows.anchor: وقد صحح هذا الحديث ابن خزيمة وابن حبان والدارقطني، والنووي في الأذكار.

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that Friday prayers are witnessed by angels and conveyed to the Prophet until the worshipper finishes; after death, the earth still cannot consume prophets’ bodies, and the Prophet lives sustained.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أكثروا الصلاة علي يوم الجمعة؛ فإنه مشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this route strange and interrupted because Ubada ibn Nasi did not meet Abu al-Darda.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث غريب من هذا الوجه، وفيه انقطاع بين عبادة بن نسي وأبي الدرداء

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة وأبو مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Abu Umama and Abu Masud a Prophetic command to increase prayers on the Prophet on Friday night and day; Ibn Kathir says both chains are weak.
rows.anchor: وقد روى البيهقي من حديث أبي أمامة وأبي مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الأمر بالإكثار

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri mursal report says the earth does not consume the body of one addressed by the Holy Spirit; Ibn Kathir grades it mursal hasan.
rows.anchor: سمعت الحسن -هو البصري -يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تأكل الأرض جسد من كلمه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i transmits a mursal Prophetic instruction to increase prayers on him on Friday and its eve.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: أخبرنا إبراهيم بن محمد، أخبرنا صفوان بن سليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Friday preacher must bless the Prophet from the pulpit in both sermons, without which the sermons are invalid; Ibn Kathir identifies this as al-Shafi'i and Ahmad's view.
rows.anchor: يجب على الخطيب أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الجمعة على المنبر في الخطبتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recommends sending blessings and peace upon the Prophet when visiting his grave.
rows.anchor: يستحب الصلاة والسلام عليه عند زيارة قبره

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever greets the Prophet receives his returned greeting after God restores his spirit.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من (9) أحد يسلم علي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's direction not to make homes graves or his grave a festival, but to pray upon him because prayers reach him wherever people are; Abu Dawud alone transmits it and al-Nawawi authenticates it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تجعلوا بيوتكم قبورا، ولا تجعلوا قبري عيدا

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: A man who visited the Prophet's grave each morning explained that he loved to greet him; Ali ibn al-Husayn cited his father and grandfather for the same instruction to pray and greet from anywhere.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين بن علي: أن رجلا كان يأتي كل غداة فيزور قبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The household report through Ali ibn al-Husayn has an unnamed narrator in its chain.
rows.anchor: في إسناده رجل مبهم لم يسم (2) وقد روي من وجه آخر مرسلا

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الحسن
rows.claim: In a mursal report, al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan sees people at the grave and forbids taking it as a festival, citing that prayers reach the Prophet wherever offered.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن بن الحسن بن علي؛ أنه رأى قوما عند القبر فنهاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir supposes al-Hasan may have reprimanded the visitors because they were behaving discourteously by raising their voices beyond need.
rows.anchor: فلعله رآهم يسيئون الأدب برفع أصواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grave visitor is told that a person in Andalusia is no farther from the Prophet than he is, since the Prophet receives everyone's prayers and blessings.
rows.anchor: يا هذا، ما أنت ورجل بالأندلس منه إلا سواء، أي: الجميع يبلغه

rows.speaker: الحسن بن الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali reports from his father the instruction to pray upon the Prophet wherever one is, since the prayer reaches him.
rows.anchor: عن حسن بن حسن بن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنهم، عن أبيه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "صلوا علي حيثما كنتم

rows.speaker: أم أنيس بنت الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: A report says God appointed two angels who ask forgiveness for anyone who prays upon the Prophet when he is mentioned, and God and His angels answer amen.
rows.anchor: عن أم أنيس بنت الحسن بن علي، عن أبيها قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أرأيت قول الله، عز وجل: {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the angel report very strange and its chain severely weak.
rows.anchor: غريب جدا، وإسناده فيه ضعف شديد (8)

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God has angels traveling the earth who convey the Muslim community's greetings to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن لله ملائكة سياحين في الأرض، يبلغوني

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report claims that prayers at the Prophet's grave are heard directly and distant prayers are conveyed; Ibn Kathir questions its chain, unique to the abandoned Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi al-Saghir.
rows.anchor: تفرد به محمد بن مروان السدي الصغير، وهو متروك، عن الأعمش، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The authors' school recommends that a pilgrim in ihram pray upon the Prophet after finishing the talbiya.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا: ويستحب للمحرم إذا لبى وفرغ من تلبيته أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad reports that a man was instructed to pray upon the Prophet whenever he completed his talbiya.
rows.anchor: عن القاسم بن محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق قال: كان يؤمر الرجل إذا فرغ من تلبيته أن يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على كل حال

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar instructs pilgrims to perform seven circuits, pray two units at the Station, then make takbirs and supplications at al-Safa and al-Marwa, including praise, blessings on the Prophet, and personal requests; Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and strong.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن وهب بن الأجدع قال: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول: إذا قدمتم فطوفوا بالبيت سبعا، وصلوا عند المقام ركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some recommend mentioning blessings on the Prophet alongside God's name at slaughter, taking support from 94:4 and an interpretation that God is never mentioned without the Prophet also being mentioned.
rows.anchor: ويستحب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع ذكر الله عند الذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority rejects that practice, holding that slaughter is a place to mention God alone, like eating, entering, and intercourse, where no Prophetic instruction to bless the Prophet exists.
rows.anchor: وخالفهم في ذلك الجمهور، وقالوا: هذا موطن يفرد فيه ذكر الرب تعالى، كما عند الأكل، والدخول، والوقاع وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report commands prayers upon God's prophets and messengers; Ibn Kathir says its chain contains two weak narrators, Umar ibn Harun and his teacher.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "صلوا على أنبياء الله ورسله؛ فإن الله بعثهم كما بعثني"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recommends praying upon the Prophet if one's ear rings, provided the report is sound.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك: أنه يستحب الصلاة عليه عند طنين الأذن، إن صح الخبر في ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports the instruction to remember and pray upon the Prophet when an ear rings and to say God remembers whoever remembers him well; Ibn Kathir calls the chain strange and questions its authenticity.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه أبي رافع (2) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا طنت أذن أحدكم فليذكرني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Writers are said to recommend repeating blessings each time they write the Prophet's name; a report from Ibn Abbas promises continuing reward while the name remains in the book.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من صلى علي في كتاب، لم تزل الصلاة جارية له ما دام اسمي في ذلك الكتاب"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Ibn Abbas report is unsound from many routes, as is an Abu Hurayra version; al-Dhahabi suspects fabrication, and versions from Abu Bakr and Ibn Abbas are also invalid.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا الحديث بصحيح من وجوه كثيرة، وقد روي من حديث أبي هريرة، ولا يصح أيضا (6)

rows.speaker: الذهبي
rows.claim: Al-Dhahabi says he suspects the report about writing blessings is fabricated.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ أبو عبد الله الذهبي شيخنا: أحسبه موضوعا

rows.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Al-Khatib reports seeing in Ahmad ibn Hanbal's handwriting that he often wrote the Prophet's name without the blessing in writing, though it reached him that Ahmad said the blessing aloud.
rows.anchor: قال: رأيت بخط الإمام أحمد بن حنبل، رحمه الله: كثيرا ما يكتب اسم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غير ذكر الصلاة عليه كتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending blessings as an appendage to blessings on the Prophet's family, wives, or descendants is permissible by consensus.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم في الحديث: "اللهم، صل على محمد وآله وأزواجه وذريته"، فهذا جائز بالإجماع

rows.speaker: قائلون
rows.claim: Some allow singling out non-prophets for blessings, citing verses about God's and the angels' blessings, prayers for believers, and Prophetic responses to almsgivers and a woman who requested prayers for herself and her husband.
rows.anchor: فقال قائلون: يجوز ذلك، واحتجوا بقوله: {هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته}

rows.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
rows.claim: The majority disallows singling out non-prophets because the formula has become a distinctive mark of prophets; they read apparent scriptural examples as supplication, and Ibn Kathir calls this a good approach.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور من العلماء: لا يجوز إفراد غير الأنبياء بالصلاة؛ لأن هذا قد صار شعارا للأنبياء إذا ذكروا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others prohibit it because blessings on non-prophets became a distinctive practice of people of innovation, whose conventions should not be followed.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: لا يجوز ذلك؛ لأن الصلاة على غير الأنبياء قد صارت من شعار أهل الأهواء

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: The three reported positions are prohibition, mild dislike, or contrary to what is preferable; al-Nawawi says the correct majority position is mild dislike because it is an innovation's emblem.
rows.anchor: حكاه الشيخ أبو زكريا النووي في كتاب الأذكار. ثم قال: والصحيح الذي عليه الأكثرون أنه مكروه كراهة تنزيه

rows.speaker: أبو محمد الجويني
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni treats the greeting like blessings: do not use it as an isolated formula for absent non-prophets, while greeting those present is unanimously permitted.
rows.anchor: وأما السلام فقال الشيخ أبو محمد الجويني من أصحابنا: هو في معنى الصلاة، فلا يستعمل في الغائب، ولا يفرد به غير الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes copyists' tendency to single out Ali with عليه السلام or كرم الله وجهه and says companions should be treated equally in honorifics; the two shaykhs and Uthman deserve them even more.
rows.anchor: أن يفرد علي، رضي الله عنه، بأن يقال: "عليه السلام"، من دون سائر الصحابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says blessings should not be said over anyone but the Prophet; Muslims should instead be prayed for with forgiveness.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس أنه قال: لا تصح

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ordered that blessings be reserved for prophets and supplication made generally for Muslims, after storytellers began giving caliphs and rulers formulas like the Prophet's; Ibn Kathir grades the report hasan.
rows.anchor: كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز، رحمه الله: أما بعد، فإن أناسا من الناس قد التمسوا الدنيا بعمل الآخرة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b tells Aisha that seventy thousand angels come by dawn and again by night to surround the Prophet's grave and pray for him, then seventy thousand accompany him at resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن كعبا دخل على عائشة، رضي الله عنها، فذكروا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال كعب: ما من فجر يطلع إلا نزل سبعون ألفا من الملائكة

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says one should combine blessings and greeting upon the Prophet rather than say only one, deriving this recommendation from the verse; the fuller formula is to bless him and greet him fully.
rows.anchor: إذا صلى على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فليجمع بين الصلاة والتسليم، فلا يقتصر على أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates and provides, and is therefore alone in divinity: the polytheists admit that only God sends rain from heaven and grows crops from earth.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى مقررا تفرده بالخلق والرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formulation is wrap-and-spread: one party is rightly guided and the other plainly astray; it cannot be that both parties share guidance or error, and the proof of divine oneness exposes their polytheism.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب اللف والنشر، أي: واحد من الفريقين مبطل، والآخر محق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Muhammad's companions told the polytheists that they were not both following one way and one of the two groups must be guided.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: قد قال ذلك أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للمشركين: والله ما نحن وإياكم على أمر واحد

rows.speaker: عكرمة وزياد بن أبي مريم
rows.claim: Ikrima and Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam explain the meaning directly: we are guided and you are plainly astray.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة وزياد بن أبي مريم: معناه: إنا نحن لعلى هدى، وإنكم لفي ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement expresses reciprocal disavowal: the groups are separate, inviting one another to God and exclusive worship; acceptance brings fellowship, while rejection leaves each disavowing the other.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون} : معناه التبري منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir connects this reciprocal disavowal to Jonah's declaration that each side is responsible for its own deeds and to the separation expressed in Surat al-Kafirun.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وإن (3) كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers all creatures on the Day of Judgment and judges justly, rewarding each person according to deeds; then the parties will know who gains victory and everlasting happiness, as 30:14–16 describes.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {قل يجمع بيننا ربنا} أي: يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fattah al-Alim means the just judge who knows the realities of matters.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى: {وهو الفتاح العليم} أي: الحاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power appears in the changing lengths of night and day: each is first lengthened as the other shortens to balance, then the process reverses, with their lengths alternating through summer and winter.
rows.anchor: ثم يأخذ من هذا في هذا، فيطول هذا ويقصر هذا، ثم يتقارضان صيفا وشتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon wording includes the moving planets and fixed piercing stars, all traveling on a precisely measured and regulated course by decree of the Mighty, Knowing God.
rows.anchor: والنجوم السيارات، والثوابت الثاقبات بأضوائهن أجرام السموات، الجميع يسيرون بمقدار معين، وعلى منهاج مقنن محرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term through which each runs is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي: إلى يوم القيامة. {ذلكم الله ربكم} أي: الذي فعل هذا هو الرب العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who ordered these works is the great Lord, and there is no deity besides Him.
rows.anchor: {ذلكم الله ربكم} أي: الذي فعل هذا هو الرب العظيم، الذي لا إله غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are rival idols fashioned in the likeness of the exalted angels whom their worshippers claim as models.
rows.anchor: {والذين تدعون من دونه} أي: من الأنداد والأصنام التي هي على صورة من تزعمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وعطاء وعطية العوفي والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, Ata, Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others explain qitmir as the thin membrane covering a date stone.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وعطاء وعطية العوفي، والحسن، وقتادة وغيرهم: القطمير: هو اللفافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols own nothing in the heavens or earth, not even the tiny amount represented by a date stone's membrane.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يملكون من السموات والأرض شيئا، ولا بمقدار هذا القطمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols do not hear invocations because they are inanimate objects with no souls.
rows.anchor: لأنها جماد لا أرواح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the idols heard, they would be unable to fulfill what their worshippers ask.
rows.anchor: ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the alleged deities disown their worshippers, as in 46:5–6 and 19:81–82, where false gods fail to answer and become enemies of their worship.
rows.anchor: {ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم} ، أي: يتبرؤون منكم، كما قال تعالى: {ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can inform you as fully as an expert about the outcomes, final consequences, and eventual destination of affairs.
rows.anchor: ولا يخبرك بعواقب الأمور ومآلها وما تصير إليه، مثل خبير بها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the expert is God Himself, whose report of what will occur is certain.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يعني نفسه تبارك وتعالى، فإنه أخبر بالواقع لا محالة
